question.problem:
Consider the function $f:{R}^{2}\to R,$ defined as

$$
f(x)={e}^{x+{y}^{2}},\,x=[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}].
$$

If the tangent to $f$ at $a=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]$ is given by

$$
z-∗=[\begin{aligned}∗ & ∗\end{aligned}]([\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}])
$$

what is the sum of the missing values?

current_example.worked_solution:
Suppose a transformation $\boldsymbol{f}:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m$ is defined by 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14196264/assets/35aa0234aa4176cf89460e49d4e1c9c8b50560be36798310226b6adb329d5389.svg) 

where $f_1,f_2,\ldots,f_m$ are scalar functions with $n$ variables. If $\boldsymbol{f}$ is differentiable at $\mathbf{x},$ then the total derivative of $\boldsymbol{f}$ at $\mathbf{x},$ denoted $\boldsymbol{f}'(\mathbf{x}),$ is given by the $m \times n$ matrix

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14196264/assets/8c585ec5d1d32af83218dc415e9691eb1c3eb8cbed8e81823e251c3711dc2469.svg)

In our case, we have the following:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14196264/assets/9b2a3447b2fd89b2d81f180d26a341810498b91d481b0b7ca6f482a6a332fce7.svg)

First, we compute the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{3}+{e}^{y})=3{x}^{2},\, & \frac{∂f}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{3}+{e}^{y})={e}^{y}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14196264/assets/c18c600e5d1a9c9bafc8f213fe1f6587789cd39a5f5e2ebe19389277b3e844c7.svg)

Evaluating $f$ and its derivative at ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14196264/assets/0529e8fa834ab82b70eded0c689a745c29a2cae739cd2fcddde5bc72a131d25c.svg) we have

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14196264/assets/69ebe02c752aea6476c11d644ae336c7ea3b0ddd1b5dc92a10624b1794029382.svg)

The tangent to $f$ at $\mathbf x = \mathbf a$ is given by

$$
z - f(\mathbf a) = \boldsymbol{f}'(\mathbf a)(\mathbf x - \mathbf a).
$$

Substituting $f(\mathbf a),$ $\boldsymbol{f}'(\mathbf a),$ and $\mathbf a$ in the equation above, we obtain

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14196264/assets/51381ae23bd8a931754e43ce66ce896561b9c1f7b9a237625fa0a00c3f2915ec.svg)
